issue.title: Check main's count-independent sum at K 33 with 2 and 3 workers, and time it

labels.name: win2
labels.description: Task for win2, the Windows desktop

issue.body:
**What.** Run main's count-independent `amp_flint_par.py` (64914d8, #246, fixed blocks) at ω/ω∞ = 1.10, K 33, J 1000, 960 bits, `--fit phys --mf 6:12`, with `--procs` 2 and 3, in a fresh worktree on main. Compare the two runs with each other, and their σ₁₆ with the three earlier values: the original code at 3 workers (#202), at 2 workers (#229, T153), and #236's per-task order (#247). Record the wall time of each against #202's and #229's. Recommended by win2 in #247's summary.

**Why.** #246 was verified only at K 17, J 200, and its cost was not measured at production size. At K 33 the summation order moves σ₁₆ by about 1.4e-18 (#247).

**Acceptance (can fail).**
- The two runs are bit for bit equal, or the first differing key is named.
- σ₁₆ lies within the spread of the earlier three values (1.4e-18), or the difference is reported.
- The wall times are reported against the original code at the same worker count.

**Depends on.** #246, #247.

comments.body: **Started, win2, 2026-11-09 19:15:09 UTC**, beside #228 and #256: 45 GB free of 95.5 GB at the start, above the 20 GB line. Fresh worktree `D:\choptuik-i263`, detached at f57c976 (main, contains #246's 64914d8), separate from the pinned checkout `D:\choptuik-large-d` (188853c, which #228 and #256 keep). Python 3.14.10 (`venv-t177`, python-flint 0.9.0 / FLINT 3.6.0), Normal priority, no affinity. The two commands at once, from `D:\choptuik-i263\solver\inner_amp\`: `amp_flint_par.py 1.10 33 1000 960 --procs N --fit phys --mf 6:12 --out I263-win2/sigF_w1.10_K33_J1000_main_procsN.json` for N = 2 and 3 (`run_i263.sh`), 5 processes in all. Expected about 3 to 4 h each under the present load (the original code took 8455 s at 3 and 11 034 s at 2 workers, the per-task order of #247 10 532 s and 13 284 s beside #228 and #256). `compare_263.py` (selftest ok) compares the two with each other, their σ₁₆ with the three earlier values against the 1.4e-18 spread, and lists the wall times. #228 and #256 keep priority for memory: if free memory falls below about 22 GB (`I256-win2/mem_watch.sh`) I run these one at a time. Hourly progress posts here. Raw folder `I263-win2/`.

**Progress, 2026-11-09 19:26 UTC (11 min after the 19:15:09 start).** Both runs of main's `amp_flint_par.py` (worktree f57c976) go on: `--procs` 2 at order 9 after 148 s, `--procs` 3 at order 9 after 131 s. Process trees 2.3 and 2.6 GB. Free memory 40.1 GB of 95.5 GB at 19:19 with #228 (14.1 GB) and #256 (8.1 GB each) beside them, above the 22 GB line of `mem_watch.sh`, so both go on at once. For the wall-time comparison, the same order 9 took 159 s with the original code at 2 workers (#229) and 152 s at 3 workers (#202), and 148 s and 134 s with #247's per-task variant; one early order says little, the full table of wall times comes with the results. `compare_263.py` (selftest ok) runs when both JSONs exist.

**Progress, 2026-11-09 20:26 UTC (1 h 11 min after the 19:15:09 start).** Both runs of main's `amp_flint_par.py` (worktree f57c976) go on, no exit. `--procs` 3 is at order 25 after 3241 s (the original code in #202 printed it at 3218 s, ratio 1.01); `--procs` 2 is at order 23 after 3275 s (the original in #229: 3008 s, ratio 1.09). #247's per-task variant took 1.2 times the original, so the fixed blocks of #246 cost far less in these two early orders, under a similar load (all four runs ran beside #228 and #256); the final times come with the results. Process trees 5.8 GB (3 workers) and 4.4 GB (2 workers). Free memory 30.0 GB of 95.5 GB at 20:16 (25.9 to 45.7 GB over the hour, lowest watch reading 24.0 GB against the 22 GB line). If the watcher fires I stop the `--procs` 2 run and rerun it after #256 ends (about 22:45 UTC); I expect `--procs` 3 to end near 21:40 UTC and `--procs` 2 near 22:35 UTC if both go on. `compare_263.py` (selftest ok) runs when both JSONs exist.

**Memory, 2026-11-09 20:45 UTC: I stopped #263's `--procs` 2 run by hand and will rerun it after #256 ends.** At 20:43:09 the alert-only watcher of #256 fired at 22 GB (free 20.9 GB of 95.5 GB, 20.5 GB at 20:44; it was 28.4 GB at 20:40), with the process trees at #228 15.3 GB, #256 11.6, 11.7 and 11.6 GB, #263 5.7 GB (3 workers) and 4.6 GB (2 workers), commit charge 79.4 of 101.5 GB, and #256's nodes at order 35 of 39 and #228 at order 33 still growing. #228 and #256 keep priority for memory (coordinator), so at 20:43:57 I ended the `--procs` 2 tree of #263 (`taskkill /T /F`, order 25 after 4317 s, 4.6 GB), which brought free memory to 25.8 GB. Nothing else was touched: #228, #256 and #263's `--procs` 3 run (order 27 after 4256 s, expected to end near 21:40 UTC) go on. The partial log is kept as `I263-win2/main_procs2_stopped_at_k25.log` and the stop is in `exits.txt`. The `--procs` 2 run restarts when #256 has ended (about 22:45 UTC) and takes about 3 h alone (`bash run_i263.sh "2"`), so the results of #263 come about 02:00 UTC; the watcher now alerts at 20 GB.

**Progress, 2026-11-09 21:20 UTC (2 h 5 min after the 19:15:09 start).** The `--procs` 3 run of main's `amp_flint_par.py` (worktree f57c976) is at order 29 after 5543 s; the original code in #202 printed order 29 at 5352 s (ratio 1.04, 1.01 at order 25), and #247's per-task variant needed 6547 s at order 29 (1.22). Expected end near 21:45 UTC (8455 s × 1.04). Process tree 5.8 GB. The `--procs` 2 run was stopped by hand at 20:43:57 (order 25 after 4317 s) when the memory alert fired (free 20.9 GB), by the coordinator's priority #228, then #256, then #263; it restarts alone as soon as #256 ends (about 22:50 UTC), 3 h alone, so its result and the full comparison come about 02:00 UTC. If the watcher (now 20 GB) fires again before 21:45, the `--procs` 3 run is stopped next and both counts are rerun after #256. Free memory 28.2 GB of 95.5 GB at 21:12 (24.8 to 37.5 GB over the hour).

**Progress, 2026-11-09 22:12 UTC. The `--procs` 3 run of main's code is done; `--procs` 2 reruns after #256 ends.** `amp_flint_par.py 1.10 33 1000 960 --procs 3` on the worktree f57c976 ended with exit 0 at 21:42:06 UTC after 8816 s (products 1320.2 s, fit setup 17.8 s, fits 7470.0 s). The original code in #202 took 8455 s (ratio 1.04) under a lighter load. Interim look at the finished file against the earlier K 33 files (timing keys and `procs` dropped; the acceptance on the two runs of main's code needs the `--procs` 2 run and is not answered yet):

| against | `sigma_str` | `sigma_err` | `f` | `fit_info` err/resid |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| original, 3 workers (#202) | **equal, σ₁₆ identical in all 20 digits** | index 16 differs (1.3203953e-26 against 1.3203952e-26) | 2 of 136 differ (first 33_3) | 52 of 153 families (first 21_19) |
| original, 2 workers (#229) | σ₁₆ by 1.48e-19 | index 16 | 3 of 136 | 57 of 153 |
| per-task order (#247) | σ₁₆ by 1.3e-18 | index 16 | 3 of 136 | 58 of 153 |

So σ₁₆ of main's code with 3 workers equals the original's 3-worker value, within the 1.4e-18 spread of the earlier three, while it is not bit for bit equal to any of those files (it is another summation order, fixed blocks). The `--procs` 2 run of main's code (stopped at 20:43:57 for memory, order 25 of 33) restarts alone as soon as #256 ends (about 22:50 UTC) and takes about 3 h; the comparison of the two runs of main's code, their σ₁₆ and the wall times follow then (about 02:00 UTC). Free memory 32.9 GB of 95.5 GB at 22:03.

**Progress, 2026-11-09 23:01 UTC (18 min after the 22:43:13 restart).** The `--procs` 2 run of main's code (worktree f57c976) runs alone now, no exit: order 13 after 393 s (the original code in #229 needed 449 s under load). Process tree 2.8 GB, free memory 67.2 GB of 95.5 GB at 22:54, beside #228 only. Expected about 3 h or less alone, near 02:00 UTC; then `compare_263.py` compares the two runs of main's code, their σ₁₆ with the three earlier values against the 1.4e-18 spread, and lists the wall times. The `--procs` 3 run (done 21:42:06, 8816 s) is already compared in the earlier comment.

**Progress, 2026-11-09 23:54 UTC (1 h 11 min after the 22:43:13 restart).** The `--procs` 2 run of main's code (worktree f57c976) runs alone beside #228, no exit: order 23 after 2822 s (the original code in #229 needed 3008 s for order 23 under load, ratio 0.94, with 4 times fewer other processes now). Process tree 4.4 GB, free memory 62.2 GB of 95.5 GB at 23:46, machine at 25 to 36% utilization. Expected end near 01:40 UTC (0.94 × 11 034 s); then `compare_263.py` compares the two runs of main's code, their σ₁₆ with the three earlier values against the 1.4e-18 spread, and lists the wall times against the original code at the same worker counts.

**Progress, 2026-11-10 00:38 UTC (1 h 55 min after the 22:43:13 restart).** The `--procs` 2 run of main's code runs beside #228 and the #268 load checks, no exit: order 27 of 33 printed after 4962 s (about 00:06 UTC, the original code in #229: 5308 s), order 29 is due now (original: 6813 s). Expected end near 01:40 UTC. Process tree 4.4 GB, free memory 64 GB of 95.5 GB at 00:30. `compare_263.py` (selftest ok) runs when the JSON is written.

**Results, win2, 2026-11-10 01:52 UTC.** `amp_flint_par.py 1.10 33 1000 960 --procs N --fit phys --mf 6:12` on main's count-independent code (#246, fixed blocks, `NBLOCK = 12`; worktree `D:\choptuik-i263` detached at f57c976, separate from the pinned checkout at 188853c), Python 3.14.10, python-flint 0.9.0 / FLINT 3.6.0, Normal priority, no affinity. `--procs` 3 ended with exit 0 after 8816 s (21:42:06 UTC), started 19:15:09 beside #228 and #256. `--procs` 2 was stopped by hand at 20:43:57 (order 25 of 33, 4317 s) when the memory watcher fired (#228 and #256 keep priority, #263 is the cheapest to redo), and rerun alone from 22:43:13 to 01:48:18 beside #228 and #268, exit 0, 11 105 s.

**Acceptance 1: the two runs are bit for bit equal. Met.** `compare_263.py` (exit 0, selftest ok), timing keys and `procs` dropped: `sigma_str`, `sigma_err`, `f`, `fit_info` and every other key of the 2-worker and 3-worker files are equal. So main's code gives the same bits for 2 and 3 workers at K 33, as #246 intends (verified only at K 17, J 200 before).

**Acceptance 2: σ₁₆ is within the spread of the earlier three values (1.41e-18). Met.** σ₁₆ of both runs is 3.3878621466602032849e-13 − 2.0036709659677382538e-13 i; `sigma_err[16]` 1.3203953e-26:

| earlier K 33 value | relative difference of σ₁₆ from main's |
|---|---|
| original code, 3 workers (#202) | **0, identical in all 20 digits** |
| original code, 2 workers (#229, T153) | 1.48e-19 |
| per-task order (#247) | 1.3e-18 |

σ₀ to σ₁₅ are equal to all 20 digits in every file. Main's file is not bit for bit equal to any earlier one: `sigma_err[16]` differs, `f` in 2 of 136 entries against #202's (3 against the others), `fit_info` err and resid in 52 of 153 families against #202's and 57 and 58 against the others. That σ₁₆ equals the 3-worker original's at the 20 stored digits, while other keys differ, is an observation; I did not look for its cause.

**Acceptance 3: wall times against the original code at the same worker count.** (`seconds` of the JSONs; the load beside each run differed: #202 ran beside the amplitude loop, #196, #195, #213 and negative-mass jobs, #229 beside #213, main's 3-worker run beside #228 and #256, its 2-worker run beside #228 and #268.)

| workers | main (#246) | original code | per-task order (#247) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 8814 s | 8454 s (#202), +4.3% | 10 531 s, +25% |
| 2 | 11 104 s | 11 033 s (#229), +0.6% | 13 283 s, +20% |

So the fixed blocks cost 0.6 to 4% in these runs, against 20 to 25% for the per-task messages of #247; the loads differ, so this is the order of magnitude, not a clean timing (a clean one needs the machine otherwise idle).

**Discrepancies:** none new. The four K 33 σ₁₆ values (original code with 3 and 2 workers, #247's per-task order, main's fixed blocks) are evaluations of the same quantity in four summation orders; their spread is 1.4e-18, about 850 times below the 1.2e-15 J 1000 truncation at 1.10 (#256).

**Raw:** `I263-win2/` at commit 870aebf of choptuik-large-d-raw plus a README fix (both JSONs, logs, the stopped run's partial log `main_procs2_stopped_at_k25.log`, `exits.txt`, `compare_263.py` and `compare_263.log`, README with the results).

**Recommended tasks:** none. A clean timing of main's code (K 25 at 1 to 4 workers on an idle machine, against the original code's) is possible if the coordinator wants the exact cost, after #228 and #268 have ended.

#263 is closed with this comment: both runs are complete and the three acceptance conditions are answered.

Closed by win2: both runs of main's code are complete, bit for bit equal, sigma_16 is within the spread, and the wall times are reported (the 2-worker run was stopped once for memory and rerun alone). The results are in the comment above.
